subject: MSA negotiation: carve-out phrasing for consequential & punitive losses
messages:

Cc: Mike Lopez <mike.lopez@horizoncare.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines attached — damages carve-outs

Michael — attaching our team’s redlines to the MSA. Two items we want to call out explicitly:

1) Consequential / special / incidental damages — we’ve proposed a one-way exclusion that protects HorizonCare for downstream losses. Our commercial team will need that to be one-way; please flag if Redwood cannot accept.

2) Punitive damages — we’ve added a carve-out that allows punitive damages to be recoverable to the extent they are awardable by law against either party (we recognize this is narrow).

We also annotated the definition of consequential to include "loss of business, loss of profits, loss of data, and third-party claims". Happy to walk through over a quick call if easier.

Attachments: MSA_HorizonCare_Redline_20280516.docx (redline)

Thanks,
Tara Hudson
Sr. Counsel, HorizonCare

Tara — thanks for the redlines. Looping in our legal team (Laura) and our agreements lead (Karthik) to confirm position. A few quick asks from our side:

- Is HorizonCare willing to accept mutual exclusion for "consequential/special/incidental" with a narrow set of carve-outs (IP indemnity, breach of confidentiality, willful misconduct)? That’s the route we normally take.
- For punitive damages, our standard is: excluded except where awardable under applicable law (i.e., cannot be contractually granted). Are you asking for one-way recoverability?

I’ve attached a draft proposal we can start from (redline_proposal_mg_20280517.docx). If you’re free I can do a 20-min call this afternoon to try to close.

Best,
Michael
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: RE: MSA redlines attached — damages carve-outs

Michael — my read and recommended negotiating posture below. (Short version: push for mutual exclusion; accept narrow, standard carve-outs.)

On Fri, May 17, 2028 at 10:03 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Tara — thanks for the redlines. Looping in our legal team...

Analysis / recommendation:
- Consequential/special/incidental: Redwood should insist on a mutual exclusion. One-way exclusions are asymmetric and create unacceptable exposure for Redwood in a SaaS context. Offer language: "Neither party will be liable to the other for any consequential, special, incidental, exemplary or punitive damages, including lost profits, lost business, loss of data or business interruption, except to the extent arising from (a) a party’s gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) breach of confidentiality obligations, or (c) infringement of the other party’s intellectual property rights."

- Punitive damages: We should keep punitive/exemplary damages excluded by contract (i.e., cannot be contracted-for) but acknowledge the limited exception "to the extent permitted by applicable law". Do not agree to a one-way carve-in for punitive damages — that exposes Redwood to statutory penalties that vary widely. Proposed wording: "Punitive, treble or exemplary damages are excluded except where such damages are awarded as a matter of law against a party in a proceeding to which that party is subject and cannot be contractually limited."

- Definition fight: If HorizonCare insists on listing specific categories (they did), propose a merged definition that captures common categories without expanding to cover third-party defense costs or statutory penalties. Avoid enumerations that pull in consequential third-party claims.

Attached: redline_proposal_mg_20280517.docx (our counterproposal)

If they push hard on one-way language commercially, suggest we trade for (i) a carve-out from the overall liability cap for IP indemnity and breach, and (ii) a higher service credit floor for breach scenarios.

Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel — Redwood Inference

If HorizonCare can accept mutual exclusion we’ll mark this as resolved and update the order form. If you need one-way language, please share what commercial concession you’d want in return (e.g., cap carve-out, longer SLA credits, or pricing discount).

Next steps:

- If you need more time, propose a 20-min call tomorrow morning.

Michael

Hi Michael / Laura — thanks for the clear proposal and the language. Per internal approvals, HorizonCare is willing to accept a mutual exclusion for consequential/special/incidental damages on the terms you proposed, provided we retain (a) an explicit example list in the definition (lost profits, third-party claims for interruption), and (b) a narrow one-way confirmation for punitive/exemplary damages only to the extent they are actually awarded by a court and arise from the party’s gross negligence or willful misconduct (we will not seek punitive damages by contract).

We appreciate the flexibility on carve-outs and can accept Redwood’s proposed exceptions for IP, confidentiality and willful misconduct. Attaching the final redline for signature: MSA_final_redline_20280518.pdf. I’ve also attached a DocuSign link for the MSA and order form.

If you can confirm we’ll counter-sign today and send the initial order form.

Best,
Tara Hudson
Sr. Counsel, HorizonCare
